title: Systems of Linear Inequalities: Graphs, Solutions and Word Problems
seo_title: Algebra 1 Systems of Inequalities Worksheets: Graphing, Shading and Word Problems (Free, Answer Key)
standard_text: Graph the solutions to a linear inequality in two variables as a half-plane (excluding the boundary in the case of a strict inequality), and graph the solution set to a system of linear inequalities in two variables as the intersection of the corresponding half-planes.
meta_desc: Free Algebra 1 systems of inequalities worksheets (A-REI.D.12): test points, match inequalities and systems to graphs with dashed or solid boundaries and shading, and write and use systems of inequalities in word problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Dashed for < or >, solid for ≤ or ≥. Shade above for > and below for <.
key_sub: The solutions of a system are where all the shadings overlap.
body_html:
How it works

To graph a linear inequality, draw the boundary line y = mx + b. Use a dashed line for < or > (points on the line are not solutions) and a solid line for ≤ or ≥. Shade above for > or ≥ and below for < or ≤, or test a point such as (0, 0).

The solution of a system of inequalities is the region where all the shadings overlap. A point is a solution only if it makes every inequality true.

Example

Is (1, 3) a solution of y ≥ x + 1 and y < −2x + 6?

3 ≥ 2 ✓.

3 < 4 ✓.

Answer: Yes

Example

Write a system: at most 10 items, and at least 3 of them are pens (p) with q pencils.

p + q ≤ 10.

p ≥ 3.

Answer: p + q ≤ 10 and p ≥ 3

Common mistakes

  • Using a solid line for < or >. Strict inequalities get a dashed line.
  • Shading the wrong side. Test a point if you are not sure.
  • Checking a point in only one inequality. It must work in all of them.
  • Mixing up “at least” (≥) and “at most” (≤).

faq.q: How do you graph a linear inequality?
faq.a: Graph the boundary line (dashed for < or >, solid for ≤ or ≥), then shade above the line for > or ≥ and below it for < or ≤.

faq.q: What is the solution of a system of inequalities?
faq.a: The region where the shaded areas of all the inequalities overlap. Every point there makes every inequality true.

faq.q: How do I know which side to shade?
faq.a: Pick a test point not on the line, such as (0, 0). If it makes the inequality true, shade its side; if not, shade the other side.

faq.q: Can a system of inequalities have no solution?
faq.a: Yes. If the shaded regions never overlap, for example with parallel lines shaded away from each other, there is no solution.

items.q: Ava works at most 20 hours a week at two jobs: x hours tutoring and y hours at a café. Which inequality shows this?
items.e: “At most” means ≤: x + y ≤ 20.

items.q: Ava earns $15 an hour tutoring and $10 an hour at the café, and wants to earn at least $240. Which inequality shows this?
items.e: “At least” means ≥: 15x + 10y ≥ 240.

items.q: A school club sells pizza slices (p) for $3 and cookies (c) for $1. It needs more than $150. Which inequality fits?
items.e: “More than” means >: 3p + c > 150.

items.q: A van holds no more than 12 people: a adults and k kids. There must be at least 2 adults. Which system fits?
items.e: No more than 12 → ≤ 12; at least 2 adults → a ≥ 2.

items.q: Why are x ≥ 0 and y ≥ 0 often included in a real-world system?
c: Amounts like hours or items cannot be negative
Because every system needs four inequalities
items.e: You cannot work −3 hours or buy −2 items, so the amounts cannot be negative.

items.q: A baker has 24 cups of flour. Bread uses 3 cups and muffins use 2 cups per batch. Which inequality shows the flour limit for b batches of bread and m batches of muffins?
items.e: Flour used must not be more than 24: 3b + 2m ≤ 24.

items.q: A theater has 300 seats. Adult tickets (a) cost $10 and child tickets (c) cost $6. It needs at least $2,400 in sales. Which system fits?
items.e: Seats: at most 300. Money: at least $2,400. a + c ≤ 300 and 10a + 6c ≥ 2,400.

items.q: Which phrase means ≥?
items.e: At least 5 means 5 or more: ≥.

items.q: Which phrase means <?
items.e: Fewer than 10 means less than 10, not including 10.

items.q: Grace needs at least 3 servings of fruit (f) and vegetables (v) together, but no more than 2 servings of fruit. Which system fits?
items.e: Together at least 3 → ≥ 3; fruit no more than 2 → f ≤ 2.
